nunchaku:F7.note: Only the upspin H8 is shown. The downspin version clips the forearm and the V8 hits the head, so both were removed. Inspin and outspin H8 are not simulated yet.

nunchaku:F9.note: The two planes are 52 cm apart, against 44 cm in the basic figure-8. The twisted figure-8 is not shown.

nunchaku:M1.note: The weight goes from foot to foot once every two swings, and the swing is simulated on the moving body.

nunchaku:M4.note: Down and up once every four swings, by bending the knees. The swing is simulated on the moving body.

nunchaku:D13.note: An upspin in one hand and a flat nearspin in the other, each simulated on its own.

nunchaku:C2.note: The swing is slowed a little, the other forearm comes up into its path, and the striker comes back the other way. How much speed the body returns (35%) is an assumed value, not a measured one.

nunchaku:A1.note: The release was chosen by search so the handle turns once and returns within reach.

nunchaku:A3.note: The release was chosen by search so the handle turns once and returns within reach.

nunchaku:A12.note: The release was chosen by search so the handle turns once and reaches the other hand, which then turns it to its own grip.

nunchaku:D14.note: The other nunchaku keeps its normal swing.

nunchaku:D16.note: Both are released at the same moment, mirrored.

nunchaku:F1.note: Thumb toward the link is the front grip; little finger toward the link is the back grip.

nunchaku:F2.note: The fingers are open and the thumb alone holds the stick against the palm.

poi:F3.note: The horizontal plane is shown overhead.

poi:B1.note: The hands are side by side with one a little in front, so the two planes sit 11 cm apart and the heads pass each other.

poi:F8.note: Both poi keep spinning forward while the weight goes from foot to foot. Turns and steps are not shown.

poi:L1.note: Loop counts follow the Home of Poi convention. The hand path is solved, so it is close to a circle but not exactly one.

poi:L2.note: Petal counts follow the Home of Poi convention. The hand path is solved, so it is close to a circle but not exactly one.

poi:L3.note: Petal counts follow the Home of Poi convention. The hand path is solved, so it is close to a circle but not exactly one.

poi:L4.note: Shown with the four-petal antispin flower at each side.

poi:L5.note: Shown with the four-petal antispin flower: the arms circle opposite ways and meet at the top and the bottom.

poi:F1.note: With the arm stretched out, the head just reaches the armpit. The other hand, which pulls the head along the arm, is left out.

staff:F2.note: In front and overhead the rotor is kept turning hand over hand. At the side one closed hand is shown.

v.note: On the side plane the figure shows one closed hand: the hand changes are left out.

staff:F4.note: Kept turning hand over hand: each hand turns the staff a little under half a turn and reaches back. The sources do not say which direction is called forward.

staff:F6.note: One closed hand is shown: the hand changes on the side plane are left out.

staff:F7.note: Kept turning hand over hand above the head.

staff:P1.note: The staff changes hands twice in every turn.

staff:M1.note: The body makes one turn, in quarter-turn steps, for every four turns of the staff.

staff:C3.note: A staff turning freely on the palm keeps its rate. Friction and the small corrections of the hand are left out.

staff:T2.note: The roll over the thumb is not shown: the staff is released level.

staff:F1.note: Ground to shoulder height is the starting length the sources give.

staff:F3.note: The marked end is the thumb end.

doublestaff:F5.note: The staff changes side each time it is level, as the sources describe. Where the hand is held was chosen by search to keep the staff clear of the arm and the body.

doublestaff:F6.note: The staff changes side each time it is level, as the sources describe.

doublestaff:T1.note: Shown with a one-hand figure 8 in each hand.

doublestaff:T2.note: On the wall plane, each staff changing side when it is level.

doublestaff:T3.note: On the wall plane; the staffs stay parallel.

doublestaff:T4.note: Each staff alternates between the inside and the outside of its arm, and the two stay parallel.

doublestaff:T5.note: The same weave with the staffs turning opposite ways.

doublestaff:T6.note: Shown with extensions, one hand a quarter of a circle ahead of the other.

doublestaff:W1.note: One staff shown. The thumb end circles in front of the body and the pinky end behind it.

doublestaff:W2.note: One staff shown. Here the thumb end is the one behind the shoulder.

doublestaff:I1.note: The marked end is the one that stays still. Finger work and the body turn are not shown.

doublestaff:I2.note: Shown on the wheel plane at each side.

doublestaff:I3.note: The marked end is the one that travels.

doublestaff:I4.note: Read from the poi definition: the staff stays in line with the arm.

doublestaff:A1.note: Shown on the wheel plane with the hand circle as wide as half the staff, so the marked end travels along one line.

doublestaff:A2.note: For a staff, four petals means one turn against each circle of the hand: each end draws two.

doublestaff:A3.note: Shown with three turns of the staff for each circle of the hand. The sources do not fix that number.

doublestaff:A8.note: The antispin with a smaller hand circle, so the ends draw ellipses.

doublestaff:A10.note: Three turns against each circle of the hand, so the same end points in at all four points.

doublestaff:A11.note: Three quarters of a turn for each quarter of the hand circle, one way and then the other. The change of direction is rounded off.

doublestaff:H1.note: The right hand isolates and the left hand antispins.

doublestaff:H6.note: The same hybrid with the hands a quarter of a circle apart.

doublestaff:J1.note: Shown with one staff, at the side. The sources do not say what makes this throw "inside".

doublestaff:J2.note: Shown with one staff and an empty catching hand, on the wall plane.

doublestaff:F1.note: The thumb end is the one usually marked.

doublestaff:F3.note: One end of each staff points at a centre point in front of the chest.

buugeng:F3.note: The arm is stretched forward and the buugeng passes on the inside of the arm, then on the outside.

buugeng:F4.note: Turned by the wrist. Which way the curves face is not specified by the sources.

buugeng:T1.note: Turned by the wrist. Which way the curves face is not specified by the sources.

buugeng:T2.note: Turned by the wrist. Which way the curves face is not specified by the sources.

buugeng:I1.note: The circle of one curve stays in one place while the hand goes round it. The finger rolls that drive it are not shown.

buugeng:F1.note: Two curved blades meet at the handle. One tip is marked.

buugeng:F2.note: The same plane names as poi.
